Hi Priyanka — thanks for the note and great to hear the team found the demo useful. I pulled together the details you asked for and sketched how we typically handle pilots moving into committed tiers. See below and attached stubs: redwood_usage_export_sample.csv (sample token export) and invoice_Q1_lineitems_stub.pdf (example invoice format).

Quick answers up-front:
- We provide per-model and per-route line items on invoices; each line includes token counts (prompt/completion), unit rate, and subtotal.
- Commit tiers (tokens/month):
  * Tier 0 (no commit): pay-as-you-go at $0.0006 / prompt-token, $0.0012 / completion-token
  * Tier 1 (250M tokens/mo): 12% discount off PAYG
  * Tier 2 (1B tokens/mo): 20% discount off PAYG + 1% annual usage credit on overage if you exceed by <10%
  * Tier 3 (3B+ tokens/mo): custom pricing (usually volume-backed rate and SLA)
- Minimum commit: we recommend a 3-month rolling commit for Tiers 1–3; true-ups happen monthly and are reconciled quarterly.

Notes on the sample export: the CSV shows UTC dates, model id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and route tags. If you want it broken down by team or workspace id, we can add that column.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review the attached invoice stub and CSV with your finance team.
2) If the tiers look viable, I can loop in our finance lead (Neha) to draft a short amendment/PO-ready statement of work showing the committed tier and expected monthly charge.
3) We can include a one-time onboarding credit (up to $15k) as a pilot incentive if procurement needs it for approvals.

I've CC'd Neha to confirm the onboarding credit and to provide the DocuSign amendment template if you want to move fast.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks for the speedy reply and the attachments. Two clarifying items from finance/procurement:  

1) For the invoice stub, can you make token unit pricing explicit per model (e.g., gpt-4o-like vs smaller open models) rather than generic prompt/completion buckets? We run cost allocation per model.
2) For the commit tiers: does the discount apply uniformly across models or only to selected model families? If mixed-model calls occur (e.g., reranker + text-gen in a single workflow), how do you apply the discount?

Also, procurement asked for an export that maps tokens to the HubSpot deal id (we call this chargeback key). Can you add a column in the CSV that shows our Deal ID or an external_id tag?

If you can produce a slightly more detailed invoice sample (per-model unit prices + a token-to-deal mapping), procurement is comfortable moving to PO and we can start onboarding next week.
